one_liner: Rust CPU 2D vector renderer (sparse strips, SIMD, optional threads); about 2.4x Skia and 4x Cairo raster speed on M1.
what_it_does: Vello CPU (crate vello_cpu, now at the repo root as vello_cpu/) is an anti-aliased 2D renderer for machines with no usable GPU. It fills and strokes kurbo paths, rectangles and glyph runs with solid colours, linear/radial/sweep gradients and images, with clip paths, layers, blend modes, masks and some filters, using a PostScript/canvas-style imaging model. The API is its own: build a RenderContext, call set_paint, fill_path or stroke_path per object, then flush() and render() into a Pixmap. It is not a drop-in for Skia or Cairo, and C/C++ code can reach it only through the author's experimental C bindings (LaurenzV/vello_cpu_c).
how_it_is_fast: Paths are flattened (kurbo's analytic quadratic subdivision, with an early exit that emits one line when a curve cannot exceed the 0.25 px tolerance and a lookup table instead of powf when estimating quad counts) and binned into 4x4 tiles. The tiles become sparse strips, a run-length encoding that keeps per-pixel coverage only along path edges and marks interior spans as cheap solid fills, so cost grows with edge length more than with area. A coarse rasterizer then builds per-wide-tile command lists, and fine rasterization composites them with SIMD code written once over the fearless_simd abstraction and dispatched at runtime (NEON, SSE4.2/AVX2/AVX-512, WASM SIMD128, scalar fallback), by default on a u8 pipeline. With the multithreading feature, path rendering and fine rasterization run on a rayon pool while the main thread does coarse rasterization.
when_to_use: Pure-Rust CPU rendering of GUI, document or SVG content where tiny-skia or raqote is the bottleneck. In the author's Blend2D-harness data on an Apple M1 Pro (2025-09-24) vello-cpu ST was faster than tiny-skia in 843 of 870 cells (geometric mean about 4.2x) and raqote in 881 of 1044 (about 2.2x) (derived from page data).

Medium to large shapes (32x32 and up) on AArch64, especially many-edge polygons and curve-heavy paths. On the M1 Pro its geometric-mean lead over Skia grows from about 1.5x at 8x8 to 3.3x at 256x256, and over Cairo from 3.2x to 4.5x (derived from page data).
Curve-heavy small shapes: on 8x8 FillFish Solid it was 2.2x faster than Blend2D in 2025-09 and 2.9x in the 2026-06-08 run (derived from page data), thanks to the curve-flattening shortcut.

Software rendering that must scale across cores: the 8-thread mode gave a geometric mean of about 4.0x over its own single-thread time on the M1 Pro (2025-09-24) and 5.3x on an i9-14900K (2026-01-22) (derived from page data).
no_std/WASM targets that need a safe, dependency-light rasteriser: the crate is #![no_std] (with alloc) and #![forbid(unsafe_code)], with a libm feature and WASM SIMD paths.
when_not_to_use: You want the fastest CPU rasteriser regardless of language: Blend2D was faster in about 95% of cells (vello-cpu ST geometric mean about 0.57x of Blend2D on M1, 0.43x on i9-14900K), and Blend2D 8T beat vello-cpu 8T in 174 of 174 cells at 256x256 in the 2026-06-08 run (derived from page data).

x86 workloads dominated by rectangles or image patterns. In the i9-14900K run Cairo 1.18.2 beat it at 256x256 on 16 tests, for example StrokeRectA Solid by about 8x, FillRectA Pattern_NN by about 3.7x and FillRectU Solid by about 1.2x (derived from page data). The README itself says x86 still has 'more room for performance improvements'.
Very small simple shapes such as icons and UI glyph-sized rectangles: the fixed 4x4 tile adds overhead, and at 8x8 AGG and JUCE beat it on aligned solid rectangles in the thesis (Figure 39).
C or C++ projects that need a supported API: the only C bindings (vello_cpu_c) say they are 'not meant for production' and exist only for the benchmark harness.
Scenes with complex filter graphs (they panic) or any filter in multi-threaded mode (unsupported), per the crate docs.

integration.form: crate (vello_cpu 0.3.0 on crates.io; Rust library, no official C API)
integration.dependencies: vello_common (kurbo/peniko geometry and paint types, fearless_simd, smallvec, guillotiere), bytemuck, hashbrown; optional png, glifo (text, default on), and rayon, crossbeam-channel, ordered-channel, thread_local for the multithreading feature
integration.platforms: Any Rust target with alloc; runtime SIMD dispatch for x86/x86-64 (SSE2 baseline, SSE4.2, AVX2, AVX-512) and AArch64 NEON; WASM SIMD128 (and relaxed SIMD) chosen at compile time; scalar fallback elsewhere; big-endian rendering fixed in 0.3.0
integration.thread_safety: A RenderContext is driven from one thread. With the multithreading feature, RenderContext::new spawns its own rayon pool of min(cores - 1, 8) worker threads plus the calling thread, and flush() must be called before render() or the program panics; issue #1798 asks to share one pool across contexts.

gotchas: The API is pre-1.0 and churns: 0.3.0 (2026-10-02) replaced CompositeMode with TargetInit, renamed pop_clip_path to pop_clip and changed glyph-run return types, and 0.1.0 replaced render_to_pixmap with render/render_with. The C bindings still call render_to_pixmap and pin a git revision (35a4279).

Turning on the multithreading feature changes the default: RenderContext::new then uses up to 8 worker threads. Create contexts with RenderSettings { num_threads: 0, .. } for single-threaded rendering, and do not create many contexts, because each one owns a thread pool.

Default rendering uses the u8 pipeline (RenderMode::OptimizeSpeed). Enable the f32_pipeline feature and OptimizeQuality when you need accuracy, for example for snapshot tests. Canvas width and height are u16, so the maximum is 65535 px.

Open sparse-strips issues include FunkyPathsScene rendering incorrectly (#1240), zero-length paths with round caps not following the SVG spec (#1450), image quality loss when downscaling more than 2x (#1289), and slow image-heavy scenes (#1427 bunnymark: 70 ms ST, 26 ms MT, versus 273 ms for Skia CPU and 8.3 ms for Skia Ganesh). Version 0.0.9 widened a winding histogram from i8 to i16 after high winding counts overflowed (PR #1673).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Vello CPU over tiny-skia or raqote when you want the fastest maintained pure-Rust CPU renderer: it beat both in most cells, tiny-skia by about 4x. Pick Blend2D instead when C/C++ is fine and peak single-thread or 8-thread speed matters, and AGG or JUCE only for very small shapes.
verified_claims_summary: In the author's ETH Zurich master's thesis (first-party, not independently reproduced), a Blend2D bl_bench fork on an Apple M1 Pro rendered 1000 unaligned 256x256 solid rectangles in 14.2 ms with vello-cpu ST, against 50.3 ms for Skia (CPU, version unstated), 21.9 ms for Cairo 1.18.4 and 10.8 ms for Blend2D 0.12.0. Rust crates were built with target-feature=+avx2 on x86 and no extra flags on ARM, and the C++ compilers and flags are not stated. Across the published result JSON it was faster than Skia in 954 of 1044 cells and Cairo in 822 of 870 (derived from page data).
status_note: Very active (vello_cpu 0.3.0 released 2026-10-02, about 5.1M crates.io downloads, 3.8M of them recent) and dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT, so it is copyable. It is still 0.x with breaking releases every few weeks, so pin the version.
measurement_notes: Read the thesis evaluation (Sections 5.1-5.4), the public bl_bench fork (backend.h/.cpp, app.cpp, backend_blend2d.cpp, backend_skia.cpp) and the vello_cpu_c bindings. The vello-cpu backend .cpp itself is in neither LaurenzV/blend2d-apps (master is its only branch) nor upstream blend2d-testing/bench, so its timed calls cannot be checked. The bindings show what it ran: RenderMode::OptimizeSpeed (u8 pipeline), Level::new() runtime SIMD detection, num_threads passed through, and render_to_pixmap as a separate call. Strokes are built with Join::Bevel and butt caps, while the Skia and Blend2D backends set only the stroke width and keep their libraries' default joins. That is a small work and geometry mismatch in the stroke tests only. Backend::run times the shape loop plus flush(). Colours come from nextRgba32() with random alpha, so opaque-occlusion shortcuts cannot skew the results. Vello's times grow with shape area as full rasterisation would (FillRectU Solid 8x8 to 256x256: 0.30 to 14.2 ms per 1000), which is consistent with render being inside the timed region. Two trends show in the later public data (derived from page data). First, between the 2025-09-24 and 2026-06-08 M1 Pro runs single-thread speed rose about 7% overall, but image-pattern rectangle fills at 128-256 px regressed by up to 37% (FillRectA Pattern_NN 256x256: 20.1 to 12.8 renders/ms). Over the same runs 8T scaling fell from 3.96x to 3.02x geomean over ST, with 15 cells where 8T was slower than ST. Second, the x86 i9-14900K run (no Skia column) shows a smaller lead over Cairo (geomean 2.75x) and outright losses on rectangle and image-pattern tests. No correctness bug or invalid measurement found behind the catalogued numbers; tier C (first-party thesis, unpublished backend code) stands.
